Earlier OpenRouter boundary probe accepted 1 input token plus max_tokens=204799. Current provider-authoritative cap remains 202752, so enforcement stays conservative.

Escalating output budget across three runs against 127.0.0.1:8000 directly: 819/700 (11.5s), 823/2200 with an explicit /no_think in the prompt (35.5s), 819/6000 (92.2s). All three consumed 100% of the output budget as chain-of-thought and never emitted a final answer; /no_think was ignored. Reasoning surfaces in content rather than a separate channel. This refutes the blanket default that `claude-litellm sync` assigns to every discovered omlx route (supports_reasoning=false, x_reasoning_efforts=[], x_reasoning_source=local-runtime-no-reasoning-routing). Raw: ~/Projects/ls-sizing-study/results/smoke_c_arm/{smoke_20260823,smoke_20260823_retry2,smoke_20260823_attempt3}.json

Same small interpretation task completed normally in 20.1s (6.1s of it model load), no reasoning leakage, answer emitted. Serves as the local text-task baseline and the contrast case for the Huihui variant measured the same day. Raw: ~/Projects/ls-sizing-study/results/smoke_c_arm/smoke_20260823_attempt4.json

The identical prompt text counted 819 prompt_tokens on Huihui-Qwen3.8-27B-oQ4e-mtp and 768 on Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct-4bit — a 6.6% spread between two models on the same local runtime. Relevant to adapterConfig.outputReservation.tokenizerHeadroom (8192), which exists to absorb exactly this class of mismatch; this is the first measured local datapoint for it. Raw: same directory, compare prompt_tokens across smoke_20260823.json and smoke_20260823_attempt4.json

Qualifies 2026-08-23-huihui-qwen38-27b-reasoning-leak, which recorded the model as never emitting an answer. Re-measured on the same interpretation task with chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking toggled: thinking-ON spent 476 output tokens, thinking-OFF answered in 53. Two abliterated 4-bit siblings that exhausted an 800-token budget with thinking ON answered in 45 with it OFF. The earlier run reached oMLX directly and therefore never received the flag the packaged routes inject. The failure is the missing enable_thinking=false, not the model. Note the packaged runtime globs that inject it matched 0 of 17 live models at the time (litellmParamsOverrides keyed Qwen3.5*/Qwen3.6* while every live id is a 3.8 or vendor-prefixed name), so no discovered route received it either.

Corrects 2026-08-23-local-tokenizer-delta-819-vs-768, which attributed the whole 819-vs-768 gap to a tokenizer difference. Most of it is a fixed thinking-template preamble. Measured on one short prompt: Huihui counts 77 prompt tokens with thinking ON and 37 with it OFF (+40 constant), while Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct-4bit counts 33 either way -- it has no thinking template, so the flag is a no-op there. On the long interpretation prompt the same pair is 783 (thinking-OFF) vs 768, i.e. a real tokenizer spread near 2%, not 6.6%. This matters for adapterConfig.outputReservation.tokenizerHeadroom because a constant per-request offset and a percentage scale differently: the template overhead does not grow with prompt size, the tokenizer spread does.

With enable_thinking=false the model completed the circuit-lab interpretation task in 10.3s and outranked Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct-4bit on accuracy: it correctly separated a stuck-high failure mode from contention on the row the Instruct model misread, and got the boundary, operating-region and signature rows right. Supports promoting this route to the packaged haiku tier. Measured by the circuit-lab session; raw in ~/Projects/ls-sizing-study/results/smoke_c_arm/.

oMLX renamed its published model ids again. Both packaged routes died: 'Huihui-Qwen3.8-27B-oQ4e-mtp' is now published as 'root4k--Huihui-Qwen3.8-27B-abliterated-oQ4e-mtp' (org prefix + abliterated tag, same oQ4e-mtp quant), and 'Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-8-bit' is now 'Qwen3.8-27B-Uncensored-8bit' (hyphen dropped). The haiku alias pointed at the first, so the haiku tier was bricked. Both still appeared in the proxy's /v1/models, so nothing downstream reported a problem; a completion returned NotFoundError from oMLX. Found sideways while answering an unrelated question, the third such rename. Fixed by renaming both routes to the served ids; check.zsh now cross-checks packaged local model ids against the runtime's /v1/models when it is reachable.

verify_tool_call_fidelity.py --live-only passed all six live gates through the deployed proxy: text SSE, Claude system text blocks, forced structured tool call, streamed input_json_delta, tool_result continuation, and the Claude adaptive-thinking/effort request shape. Qualifies the route for multi-step tool-driven agentic work (the tool_result continuation gate is the multi-turn edit loop). Route carries enable_thinking=false from the '*Qwen3.8*' glob override; the forced-tool gate is the one that regressed to reasoning text when thinking was left on.

Throughput and concurrency measured through the proxy on a 28-token prompt generating 110 tokens: 1.8s and 1.7s serially (~63 tok/s output). Two concurrent identical requests completed in 4.4s wall, versus ~3.5s for the same two run back to back -- so oMLX does not serve them in parallel and concurrency is ~26% WORSE than serial. Consequence: a second consumer of :8000 cannot be isolated by concurrency, only by time-sharing. Caveat: short prompt; sustained long-context agentic runs will show lower tok/s, and an earlier long-context observation put it nearer 40 tok/s.
